Recommended isolation: capture one forward pass’s sequence outputs, then compare the production readout against an independent gather from that same tensor. For nonzero item IDs, compute `idx = torch.where(sequence.ne(0), torch.arange(L, device=sequence.device), -1).amax(1)`; gather at `idx.clamp_min(0)` and explicitly replace empty-history rows with the defined fallback, such as zeros. Never use `count_nonzero-1` for left padding. Test empty, singleton, mixed-length and full-length histories, asserting indices exactly. If aligned valid outputs pass but readouts fail, inspect indexing, empty-row handling and post-GRU transformations first. [Gather semantics](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.gather).

Distinguish raw GRU outputs from transformed recommendation features. For a dense, unidirectional, batch-first GRU, `output[:, -1, :]` corresponds to the top-layer final state `h_n[-1]`; `batch_first` does not change hidden-state layout. Packing changes endpoint handling, and ordinary GRUs still process zero-valued padding through their recurrent equations. Compare identical padding and initial states before testing padding invariance. Run `model.eval()` plus inference mode; functional dropout must explicitly use `training=self.training`, since its default is `True`. [GRU documentation](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.GRU.html), [functional dropout](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/generated/torch.nn.functional.dropout.html).

Separate same-pass readout tests from batched-versus-individual execution tests. PyTorch documents numerical differences across batching shapes; a 1e-4–6e-4 discrepancy alone proves neither correctness nor a defect. Retain existing tolerances, report maximum errors at each stage, and isolate backend/precision effects using controlled reruns and float64 references. Leave unresolved failures visible; establish correctness before attributing gains to adaptive retention. [Numerical accuracy](https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/blob/main/docs/source/notes/numerical_accuracy.md).
